rationales.1: Right-aligned prices, seasonal drawers, and filter chips make the desktop list fast to scan, but on mobile two entries collapse into one-word-per-line columns that badly slow reading.
rationales.2: Inline steppers and Add buttons follow ordinary commerce convention, yet the controls are very small and the price-pending note collides with the price column on the sweet pea row, which slightly muddies the money path.
rationales.3: This is the most explicit honesty in the set: out-of-stock lines stay listed with a restock explanation, germination sources are declared in a footer, the null price says ask us and we will write when it is set, and UK-only shipping leads both pages.
rationales.4: The tiny minus, plus, and Add targets on both surfaces and the squeezed mobile text columns are exactly wrong for older readers on tablets, despite otherwise legible body type.
rationales.5: The mobile catalog's broken one-word columns and the awkward sweet pea and carrot column widths on desktop are visible craft failures inside an otherwise disciplined system.
rationales.6: The at-a-glance stat row, sowing table, and companions with planting reasons give strong decision support, and the growing notes anticipate the beginner's doubt about the quiet first month.
rationales.7: The potting bench with seasonal drawers is a true two-person signature that reaches all the way into product copy, where the packet sits in the winter drawer of the bench.
rationales.8: The metaphor stays in the brand layer and mechanics remain conventional, though the design-study disclaimer in the footer is an odd frame break a real shop would never print.
rationales.9: Phrases like the easiest drawer on the bench and if it is listed, we can vouch for it are unmistakably this shop's voice, warm and specific throughout.
rationales.10: Season sections and chips answer the what-can-I-sow-now visit well and both surfaces share the bench frame, but the mobile layout defects tax exactly the quick repeat check this criterion rewards.
